newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish insurers show lower total nine month net.
newsitem.headline: Polish insurers show lower total nine month net.

text.p: Poland's insurance sector netted 106.3 million zlotys in the first three quarters of 1996, down from 107.7 million zlotys in the same period last year, the Central Statistical Office (GUS) said on Wednesday.
GUS said in a report that 17 insurance companies showed net profit, which totalled 182.4 million zlotys, and 25 firms suffered losses, which amounted to 74.6 million zlotys.
GUS said the lower profit resulted from a 41-percent increase in damages payouts and a 64-percent growth of insurance operating costs.
The companies had a 151.8 million gross profit in the first three quarters against 148.4 million in the corresponding period last year.

GUS also reported that life insurance firms' net totalled 70.9 million zlotys over the period, down from 78 million zlotys in the first three quarters of 1995. Four companies reported profit and 10 losses.
The insurers' gross premium rose by 43.7 percent to 6.1 billion zlotys, GUS said.
